newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Mer fund to relax borrowing policy.
newsitem.headline: China Mer fund to relax borrowing policy.

text.p: China Merchants China Direct Investments Ltd said on Friday it proposed to relax its borrowing policy, in a move to seek external funding to finance further investments as and when required.
The investment fund said it proposed to relax the policy of no borrowing when company liabilities exceed 25 percent of the net asset value of the company, to 50 percent.
"The proposed amendment will effectively increase the existing limit imposed on permitted borrowings," the company said in a statement.

Based on the unaudited management accounts as at March 31, 1997, the company said it had invested US$75.1 million in 12 unlisted projects in China and US$5.7 million in listed securities, representing 76 percent of the company's net assets.
"The company is in the process of evaluating a number of additional investments and the directors anticipate that the company will be fully invested before the end of 1997," it said.
"It is therefore the company's intention to seek external funding to finance further investments," it added.
The company said its investments were held as long term investment and it was appropriate that the restriction on the use of permittted borrowings for short-term funding be lifted.
